headline: Komyshuvakha aid-centre strike toll revised 33 -> 37 killed, 59 missing
dek: The death toll from Russia's Nov 2 double-tap bombing of the former school/aid distribution point and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, has risen from 33 (0600-03) to 37 confirmed dead, with 59 people missing; only 12 of the 37 bodies had been identified by Wednesday midday, further…
sources: Zaporizhzhia regional officials (acting regional military administration head Mykhailo Semikin; regional defence council co-head Ivan Fedorov) via AP and Reuters
fault_line: Deliberate double-tap on civilians vs. a legitimate strike on a military aid hub

sections.what_happened: The death toll from Russia's Nov 2 double-tap bombing of the former school/aid distribution point and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, has risen from 33 (0600-03) to 37 confirmed dead, with 59 people missing; only 12 of the 37 bodies had been identified by Wednesday midday, further identification likely requiring DNA testing. Rescuers were still searching the rubble. Russia's Nov 4 strikes also hit power stations in Kyiv and Zhytomyr regions and a cargo vessel near Odesa (already recorded in 1500-03).
sections.what_verified: AP (T1) + Reuters (T1) = 2 distinct publisher families, consistent figures. CNN (unlisted tier in this check; not counted) adds the identification detail.
sections.what_disputed: Russia's Defence Ministry says the strike targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, killing up to 25 servicemen; both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.
sections.why_matters: Toll-card update to the Komyshuvakha file (0500-03, 0600-03), not a new Short: the strike itself is Nov 2 news; what is new is the confirmed count. Demand is low — social echo found was small (Threads repost 5 likes; Facebook rescue video 17 likes, 4 comments) and no hot Reddit thread was found for the topic in this scan's check.
